claim: Fusion of intracellular trafficking vesicles is mediated by the assembly of SNARE proteins into membrane-bridging complexes.
source: Fusion of intracellular trafficking vesicles is mediated by the assembly of SNARE proteins into membrane-bridging complexes.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citation to Südhof and Rothman, 2009 in the Introduction.

claim: SNARE-mediated membrane fusion requires Sec1/Munc18-family (SM) proteins.
source: SNARE-mediated membrane fusion requires Sec1/Munc18-family (SM) proteins, SNARE chaperones that can function as templates to catalyze SNARE complex assembly.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citation to Baker and Hughson, 2016 in the Introduction.

claim: SM proteins can function as templates to catalyze SNARE complex assembly.
source: SNARE-mediated membrane fusion requires Sec1/Munc18-family (SM) proteins, SNARE chaperones that can function as templates to catalyze SNARE complex assembly.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baker et al., 2015 and Jiao et al., 2018 in the Introduction.

claim: The SM protein Munc18-1 traps the Qa-SNARE protein syntaxin-1 in an autoinhibited closed conformation.
source: Paradoxically, the SM protein Munc18-1 traps the Qa-SNARE protein syntaxin-1 in an autoinhibited closed conformation.
evidence: This is supported by the crystal structure of Munc18-1 bound to syntaxin-1 (Misura et al., 2000) discussed in the Introduction.

claim: Vps45 holds Tlg2 in an open conformation, with its SNARE motif disengaged from its Habc domain and its linker region unfolded.
source: Strikingly, Vps45 holds Tlg2 in an open conformation, with its SNARE motif disengaged from its Habc domain and its linker region unfolded.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure of Vps45-Tlg2 presented in this study.

claim: The domain 3a helical hairpin of Vps45 is unfurled, exposing the presumptive R-SNARE binding site to allow template complex formation.
source: The domain 3a helical hairpin of Vps45 is unfurled, exposing the presumptive R-SNARE binding site to allow template complex formation.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and compared to other SM protein structures.

claim: Tlg2 has a pronounced tendency to form homo-tetramers.
source: Although Tlg2 has a pronounced tendency to form homo-tetramers, Vps45 can rescue Tlg2 tetramers into stoichiometric Vps45–Tlg2 complexes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography and analytical ultracentrifugation experiments.

claim: Vps45 can rescue Tlg2 tetramers into stoichiometric Vps45–Tlg2 complexes.
source: Although Tlg2 has a pronounced tendency to form homo-tetramers, Vps45 can rescue Tlg2 tetramers into stoichiometric Vps45–Tlg2 complexes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-course size exclusion chromatography experiments showing conversion of oligomers to 1:1 complexes.

claim: SM proteins can engage Qa-SNAREs using at least two different modes, one in which the SNARE is closed and one in which it is open.
source: Our findings demonstrate that SM proteins can engage Qa-SNAREs using at least two different modes, one in which the SNARE is closed and one in which it is open.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from comparing the Vps45-Tlg2 structure (open) with the Munc18-Stx structure (closed).

claim: Most SNAREs are tail-anchored membrane proteins.
source: Most SNAREs are tail-anchored membrane proteins, and they drive fusion by forming membrane-bridging complexes that draw the vesicle and target membranes into close apposition.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: SNAREs drive fusion by forming membrane-bridging complexes that draw the vesicle and target membranes into close apposition.
source: Most SNAREs are tail-anchored membrane proteins, and they drive fusion by forming membrane-bridging complexes that draw the vesicle and target membranes into close apposition.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Fasshauer et al., 1998; Kloepper et al., 2007; Sutton et al., 1998.

claim: SNARE motifs are conserved regions about 65 residues in length.
source: Essential for this process are conserved regions about 65 residues in length called SNARE motifs, which in most SNAREs are immediately adjacent to a C-terminal transmembrane anchor.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: In most SNAREs, SNARE motifs are immediately adjacent to a C-terminal transmembrane anchor.
source: Essential for this process are conserved regions about 65 residues in length called SNARE motifs, which in most SNAREs are immediately adjacent to a C-terminal transmembrane anchor.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Four complementary SNARE motifs—one each from the R-, Qa-, Qb-, and Qc-SNARE groups—zipper together to form a parallel α-helical bundle.
source: Four complementary SNARE motifs—one each from the R-, Qa-, Qb-, and Qc-SNARE groups—zipper together to form a parallel α-helical bundle (Fasshauer et al., 1998; Kloepper et al., 2007; Sutton et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: SNARE motifs are grouped according to the zero-layer residue in the middle of the motif, either arginine (R) or glutamine (Q).
source: SNARE motifs are grouped according to the zero-layer residue in the middle of the motif, either arginine (R) or glutamine (Q).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: The four zero-layer residues interact within the otherwise hydrophobic core of the assembled SNARE bundle to help prevent out-of-register assembly of the four α-helices.
source: The four zero-layer residues interact within the otherwise hydrophobic core of the assembled SNARE bundle to help prevent out-of-register assembly of the four α-helices.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: SM proteins function as SNARE chaperones, capable of both inhibiting and catalyzing the assembly of fusogenic SNARE complexes.
source: SM proteins function as SNARE chaperones, capable of both inhibiting and catalyzing the assembly of fusogenic SNARE complexes.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Baker and Hughson, 2016.

claim: In the closed conformation of syntaxin-1, the three-helix bundle Habc domain folds back onto the SNARE motif, preventing the SNARE motif from entering into a SNARE complex.
source: In this closed conformation, the three-helix bundle Habc domain of Stx folds back onto the SNARE motif, preventing the SNARE motif from entering into a SNARE complex.
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure of Munc18-Stx (Misura et al., 2000).

claim: The closed conformation of the Qa-SNARE syntaxin-1 is wedged into a large cleft in the SM protein Munc18-1.
source: The closed conformation of the Qa-SNARE is wedged into a large cleft in the SM protein and requires the intervention of a third protein—Munc13-1—for opening (Ma et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure of Munc18-Stx (Misura et al., 2000).

claim: The closed conformation of syntaxin-1 requires the intervention of Munc13-1 for opening.
source: The closed conformation of the Qa-SNARE is wedged into a large cleft in the SM protein and requires the intervention of a third protein—Munc13-1—for opening (Ma et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ma et al., 2011.

claim: The extreme N-terminal region of syntaxin-1, termed the N-peptide, binds to a distinct site on the outside of the SM protein Munc18-1.
source: Finally, the extreme N-terminal region of Stx, termed the N-peptide, binds to a distinct site on the outside of the SM protein (Burkhardt et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Burkhardt et al., 2008.

claim: Munc18 makes direct contact with three different regions—the N-peptide, the Habc domain, and the SNARE motif—distributed along the entire length of the syntaxin-1 cytoplasmic domain.
source: Munc18 thus makes direct contact with three different regions—the N-peptide, the Habc domain, and the SNARE motif—distributed along the entire length of the Stx cytoplasmic domain.
evidence: This is based on the crystal structure of Munc18-Stx.

claim: The SM protein Vps33 binds the SNARE motifs of the Qa-SNARE Vam3 and the R-SNARE Nyv1 at adjacent sites.
source: These structures showed that the SM protein Vps33 binds the SNARE motifs of the Qa-SNARE Vam3 and the R-SNARE Nyv1 at adjacent sites.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Baker et al., 2015.

claim: In the Vps33–Vam3–Nyv1 template complex model, the two SNARE motifs adopt a half-zippered configuration, in which their N-terminal halves up to the zero layer are aligned for assembly.
source: In it, the two SNARE motifs adopt a half-zippered configuration, in which their N-terminal halves up to the zero layer are aligned for assembly.
evidence: This is based on combining crystal structures from Baker et al., 2015.

claim: Single-molecule force microscopy studies confirmed that the SM proteins Vps33, Munc18, and Munc18-3 all form template complexes with their cognate R- and Qa-SNAREs.
source: Single-molecule force microscopy studies confirmed that the SM proteins Vps33, Munc18, and Munc18-3 all form template complexes with their cognate R- and Qa-SNAREs, and that these template complexes likely represent rate-limiting intermediates in SM-catalyzed SNARE complex assembly (Jiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiao et al., 2018.

claim: Template complexes likely represent rate-limiting intermediates in SM-catalyzed SNARE complex assembly.
source: Single-molecule force microscopy studies confirmed that the SM proteins Vps33, Munc18, and Munc18-3 all form template complexes with their cognate R- and Qa-SNAREs, and that these template complexes likely represent rate-limiting intermediates in SM-catalyzed SNARE complex assembly (Jiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Jiao et al., 2018.

claim: Vps45, Tlg2 and its cognate SNAREs, and the CATCHR-family tethering complex GARP all function in trafficking from the endosome to the trans-Golgi network.
source: Vps45, Tlg2 and its cognate SNAREs, and the CATCHR-family tethering complex GARP all function in trafficking from the endosome to the trans-Golgi network (Abeliovich et al., 1998; Conibear and Stevens, 2000; Holthuis et al., 1998; Pérez-Victoria and Bonifacino, 2009; Siniossoglou and Pelham, 2001; Siniossoglou and Pelham, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In the crystal structure of the Vps45–Tlg2 complex, Vps45 makes direct contact with the N-peptide, Habc domain, and SNARE motif of Tlg2.
source: In the crystal structure of the Vps45–Tlg2 complex, Vps45 makes direct contact with the N-peptide, Habc domain, and SNARE motif of Tlg2.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure presented in this study.

claim: In the Vps45–Tlg2 complex, the Habc domain does not pack against the N-terminal region of the SNARE motif and instead appears to leave it free to initiate SNARE complex assembly.
source: In contrast with the Munc18–Stx complex, however, the bound Qa-SNARE adopts an open conformation. Specifically, the Habc does not pack against the N-terminal region of the SNARE motif and instead appears to leave it free to initiate SNARE complex assembly.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and inferred from the structural comparison.

claim: Qa-SNARE clamping may be a specialized property of Munc18, rather than a general property shared broadly among SM proteins.
source: Thus, Qa-SNARE clamping may be a specialized property of Munc18, rather than a general property shared broadly among SM proteins.
evidence: This is inferred from the comparison between the Vps45-Tlg2 structure (open) and the Munc18-Stx structure (closed).

claim: Tlg2, but not Vps45–Tlg2, is prone to homo-oligomerization.
source: Tlg2, but not Vps45–Tlg2, is prone to homo-oligomerization.
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography and analytical ultracentrifugation experiments.

claim: SM proteins can prevent SNARE misassembly and template proper assembly.
source: Taken together, our results underscore the ability of SM proteins to prevent SNARE misassembly and template proper assembly.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural and biochemical data presented in the study.

claim: There are four families of SM protein—Sec1/Munc18, Sly1, Vps33, and Vps45.
source: There are four families of SM protein—Sec1/Munc18, Sly1, Vps33, and Vps45—and every eukaryote has at least one member of each family (Kloepper et al., 2007; Koumandou et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kloepper et al., 2007 and Koumandou et al., 2007.

claim: Every eukaryote has at least one member of each SM protein family.
source: There are four families of SM protein—Sec1/Munc18, Sly1, Vps33, and Vps45—and every eukaryote has at least one member of each family (Kloepper et al., 2007; Koumandou et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kloepper et al., 2007 and Koumandou et al., 2007.

claim: Crystal structures have been reported for representatives of the Munc18, Sly1, and Vps33 families.
source: Crystal structures have been reported for representatives of the Munc18, Sly1, and Vps33 families (Baker et al., 2013; Baker et al., 2015; Bracher et al., 2000; Bracher and Weissenhorn, 2002; Burkhardt et al., 2008; Burkhardt et al., 2011; Colbert et al., 2013; Graham et al., 2013; Hackmann et al., 2013; Hu et al., 2011; Hu et al., 2007; Misura et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The crystal structure of Vps45 from Chaetomium thermophilum was refined to 2.0 Å resolution.
source: We began, therefore, by determining the crystal structure of a member of the fourth family, Vps45 from the thermotolerant fungus Chaetomium thermophilum, and refining it to 2.0 Å resolution (Table 1).
evidence: This is reported in the Results section and Table 1.

claim: Vps45 exhibits a three-domain architecture with a large cleft between domains 1 and 3a.
source: Like the other structurally characterized SM proteins, Vps45 exhibits a three-domain architecture with a large cleft between domains 1 and 3a (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Three surface regions are particularly well conserved among members of the Vps45 family.
source: Three surface regions are particularly well conserved among members of the Vps45 family, presumably because they are functionally important (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A using ConSurf analysis.

claim: The first conserved region on Vps45 corresponds to the walls of the cleft.
source: The first conserved region corresponds to the walls of the cleft.
evidence: This is observed in the structure and conservation analysis.

claim: The second and third conserved surface regions on Vps45 correspond to the N-peptide and R-SNARE binding sites observed in previous structures.
source: The second and third conserved surface regions correspond to the N-peptide and R-SNARE binding sites observed in previous structures (Baker et al., 2015; Bracher and Weissenhorn, 2002; Burkhardt et al., 2008; Hu et al., 2011; Hu et al., 2007).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison with previous structures and supported by citations.

claim: Each of the surface regions known to engage SNARE proteins in one or more of the other SM families is highly conserved in the Vps45 family.
source: Thus, each of the surface regions known to engage SNARE proteins in one or more of the other SM families is highly conserved in the Vps45 family.
evidence: This is inferred from the conservation analysis and comparison with other SM protein structures.

claim: Bacterial co-expression of C. thermophilum Vps45 and C. thermophilum Tlg2 residues 1–310 yielded a stable 1:1 complex.
source: Bacterial co-expression of C. thermophilum Vps45 and C. thermophilum Tlg2 residues 1–310, including all but the C-terminal 17 residues of the Tlg2 cytoplasmic domain, yielded a stable 1:1 complex.
evidence: This is reported in the Results section.

claim: Small crystals of Vps45–Tlg2(1-310) were obtained that diffracted to about 3.5 Å resolution.
source: Small crystals were obtained that diffracted to about 3.5 Å resolution.
evidence: This is reported in the Results section.

claim: Better crystals of Vps45–Tlg2, diffracting to 2.8 Å resolution, were obtained after deleting Tlg2 residues 201–228.
source: Better crystals, diffracting to 2.8 Å resolution, were obtained after deleting Tlg2 residues 201–228, which are missing from the otherwise nearly identical Chaetomium globosum Tlg2 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is reported in the Results section and Table 1.

claim: The deleted segment (Tlg2 residues 201–228) is located near the beginning of the 58-residue linker that connects the Habc domain and the SNARE motif.
source: The deleted segment is located near the beginning of the 58-residue linker that connects the Habc domain and the SNARE motif.
evidence: This is reported in the Results section.

claim: The structures of Vps45–Tlg2(1-310) and Vps45–Tlg2(1-310, Δ201-228) were determined by molecular replacement with Vps45 as a search model.
source: The structures of the Vps45–Tlg21-310 and Vps45–Tlg21-310, Δ201-228 complexes were determined by molecular replacement with Vps45 as a search model (Table 1).
evidence: This is reported in the Results section.

claim: There were no significant differences between the Vps45–Tlg2(1-310) and Vps45–Tlg2(1-310, Δ201-228) structures.
source: Because there were no significant differences between the two structures, we focus hereafter on the higher resolution Vps45–Tlg21-310, Δ201-228 (henceforth simply Vps45–Tlg2) structure (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is reported in the Results section.

claim: All of the well-characterized regions of Tlg2 (N-peptide, Habc domain, and SNARE motif) are visible and interact directly with Vps45.
source: All of the well-characterized regions of Tlg2 are visible and interact directly with Vps45: the N-peptide, the Habc domain, and the SNARE motif.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The sequences connecting the N-peptide, Habc domain, and SNARE motif of Tlg2, as well as the C-terminus of the SNARE motif, appear to be disordered based on the lack of interpretable electron density.
source: The sequences connecting these regions, as well as the C-terminus of the SNARE motif, appear to be disordered based on the lack of interpretable electron density.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The corresponding regions were likewise disordered in the Munc18–Stx complex, with the important exception of the linker between the Habc domain and the SNARE motif.
source: The corresponding regions were likewise disordered in the Munc18–Stx complex, with the important exception of the linker between the Habc domain and the SNARE motif, which will be discussed below.
evidence: This is based on comparison with the Munc18-Stx structure.

claim: Vps45 does not undergo a major conformational change when it binds to Tlg2.
source: Comparing the Vps45 and Vps45–Tlg2 structures reveals that Vps45 does not undergo a major conformational change when it binds to Tlg2.
evidence: This is observed by comparing the two crystal structures.

claim: The cleft in Vps45 opens up slightly, via small rotations of domains 1 and 3a relative to the rest of Vps45, in order to accommodate Tlg2.
source: The cleft does, however, open up slightly, via small rotations of domains 1 and 3a relative to the rest of Vps45, in order to accommodate Tlg2 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the Vps45 and Vps45-Tlg2 structures shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The N-peptide of Tlg2 (residues 1–14) binds to the outside of Vps45 domain 1.
source: The N-peptide of Tlg2 (residues 1–14) binds to the outside (as opposed to the cleft side) of Vps45 domain 1 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The N-peptide binding mode of Vps45, in which residues 6–12 form a short α-helix, resembles that observed previously for the Munc18 and Sly1 families of SM protein.
source: The N-peptide binding mode of Vps45, in which residues 6–12 form a short α-helix, resembles that observed previously for the Munc18 and Sly1 families of SM protein.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison with previous structures.

claim: The interaction between the Tlg2 N-peptide and Vps45 buries 870 Å2 of surface accessible area.
source: The interaction between the Tlg2 N-peptide and Vps45 buries 870 Å2 of surface accessible area.
evidence: This is calculated from the crystal structure.

claim: Arg residues at Tlg2 positions 3, 5, and 13 appear to play especially important roles in N-peptide binding, each forming both H-bonds and salt bridges with Vps45.
source: Arg residues at Tlg2 positions 3, 5, and 13 appear to play especially important roles, each of them forming both H-bonds and salt bridges with Vps45, while Tyr 9 is completely buried in a deep pocket in which its hydroxyl group forms a charge-stabilized H-bond.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Tlg2 Tyr 9 is completely buried in a deep pocket in Vps45 in which its hydroxyl group forms a charge-stabilized H-bond.
source: Arg residues at Tlg2 positions 3, 5, and 13 appear to play especially important roles, each of them forming both H-bonds and salt bridges with Vps45, while Tyr 9 is completely buried in a deep pocket in which its hydroxyl group forms a charge-stabilized H-bond.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Previous site-directed mutagenesis supports the importance of Arg 3, Tyr 9 (often Phe), and Arg 13 for high-affinity Vps45–Tlg2 binding.
source: Previous site-directed mutagenesis supports the importance of Arg 3, Tyr 9 (often Phe), and Arg 13 for high-affinity Vps45–Tlg2 binding (Burkhardt et al., 2008; Carpp et al., 2006; Dulubova et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous mutagenesis studies.

claim: Layers 0 to +4 of the Tlg2 SNARE motif interact with the opposite, cleft-facing side of Vps45 domain 1.
source: Near the other end of the Tlg2 polypeptide chain, layers 0 to +4 of the SNARE motif interact with the opposite, cleft-facing side of Vps45 domain 1 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The interaction between layers 0 to +4 of the Tlg2 SNARE motif and Vps45 domain 1 buries about 930 Å2 surface accessible area.
source: This interaction buries about 930 Å2 surface accessible area.
evidence: This is calculated from the crystal structure.

claim: The +2 and +3 layers of the Tlg2 SNARE motif form a short α-helix (H3c), with the +2 layer Ile (residue 295) fitting snugly into a deep hydrophobic pocket on Vps45 domain 1.
source: As previously observed in the Munc18–Stx complex (and also in the complex between Vps33 and the Vam3 SNARE motif), the +2 and +3 layers of the Qa-SNARE form a short α-helix (H3c), with the +2 layer Ile (residue 295 in Tlg2) fitting snugly into a deep hydrophobic pocket on domain 1 (Baker et al., 2015; Misura et al., 2000).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and compared to previous structures.

claim: Two short regions at opposite ends of Tlg2, the N-peptide and the H3c helix, bind to opposite sides of Vps45 domain 1 in a manner that closely resembles the Munc18–Stx complex.
source: In sum, two short regions at opposite ends of Tlg2, the N-peptide and the H3c helix, bind to opposite sides of Vps45 domain 1 in a manner that closely resembles the Munc18–Stx complex.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of the Vps45-Tlg2 structure with the Munc18-Stx structure.

claim: The intervening regions of Tlg2—comprising the Habc domain, the linker that connects Habc and the SNARE motif, and the N-terminal half of the SNARE motif—adopt a novel open conformation.
source: By contrast, the intervening regions of Vps45—comprising the Habc domain, the linker that connects Habc and the SNARE motif, and the N-terminal half of the SNARE motif—adopt a novel open conformation.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and compared to previous structures.

claim: Instead of folding with the SNARE motif to form a four-helix bundle-like structure, the Habc domain of Tlg2 makes a limited contact with the SNARE motif, centered around the −2 layer of the latter and at an approximately 45° angle.
source: Instead of folding with the SNARE motif to form a four-helix bundle-like structure, the Habc domain of Tlg2 makes a limited contact with the SNARE motif, centered around the −2 layer of the latter and at an approximately 45° angle.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 3A.

claim: There is no interpretable electron density for the linker connecting the Habc domain and the SNARE motif in the Vps45-Tlg2 structure.
source: As noted above, there is no interpretable electron density for the linker connecting the Habc domain and the SNARE motif, which in the Munc18–Stx complex forms a short helix that packs at right angles against the closed Habc-SNARE motif four-helix bundle (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The linker region between the Habc domain and SNARE motif has long been recognized as critical for syntaxin-1 opening and the initiation of SNARE assembly.
source: This is particularly notable inasmuch as this region has long been recognized as critical for Stx opening and the initiation of SNARE assembly (Dulubova et al., 1999; Lai et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2011; Misura et al., 2000; Munson et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The Habc domain interacts with the cleft side of Vps45 domain 1, burying 680 Å2 surface accessible area in an interaction that is largely hydrophobic in nature.
source: The Habc domain interacts with the cleft side of Vps45 domain 1, burying 680 Å2 surface accessible area in an interaction that is largely hydrophobic in nature (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Compared to the Munc18–Stx complex, the C-terminal end of the Habc domain has swung away from the SM protein, rotating approximately 15° around an axis near the N-terminal end of the domain.
source: Compared to the Munc18–Stx complex, the C-terminal end of the Habc domain has swung away from the SM protein, rotating approximately 15° around an axis near the N-terminal end of the domain (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the structures shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: As a consequence of the Habc domain rotation, the Habc domain does not make contact with Vps45 domain 3a.
source: As a consequence, the Habc domain does not make contact with domain 3a.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The N-terminal half of the Tlg2 SNARE motif forms a helix (H3a) that engages in a limited interaction with the fully extended domain 3a helical hairpin of Vps45.
source: Finally, the N-terminal half of the SNARE motif, in lieu of bundling with the Habc domain, forms a helix (H3a) that engages in a limited interaction with the fully extended domain 3a helical hairpin of Vps45 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The interaction between the Tlg2 SNARE motif helix H3a and the Vps45 domain 3a helical hairpin buries a surface accessible area of about 300 Å2.
source: This interaction buries a surface accessible area of about 300 Å2, with the −4 and −5 layer residues of H3a packing against the long helix of the hairpin.
evidence: This is calculated from the crystal structure.

claim: The −4 and −5 layer residues of Tlg2 H3a pack against the long helix of the Vps45 domain 3a hairpin.
source: This interaction buries a surface accessible area of about 300 Å2, with the −4 and −5 layer residues of H3a packing against the long helix of the hairpin.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure.

claim: H3a is rotated approximately 120° around its long axis relative to the Munc18–Stx complex.
source: As a result, H3a is rotated approximately 120° around its long axis relative to the Munc18–Stx complex (right-hand panels of Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the structures shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: The Vps45–Tlg2 structure establishes that SM proteins can engage the N-peptide, the Habc domain, and the SNARE motif of a cognate Qa-SNARE without simultaneously clamping that SNARE in a closed conformation.
source: Overall, the Vps45–Tlg2 structure establishes that SM proteins can engage the N-peptide, the Habc domain, and the SNARE motif of a cognate Qa-SNARE without simultaneously clamping that SNARE in a closed conformation.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the structural data.

claim: The domain 3a helical hairpin plays a key role in SM protein function.
source: The domain 3a helical hairpin (Figure 1A) plays a key role in SM protein function (Baker et al., 2015; Boyd et al., 2008; Hu et al., 2011; Jiao et al., 2018; Parisotto et al., 2014; Sitarska et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: In Vps45 alone, the distal tip of the helical hairpin is disordered.
source: In Vps45 alone, the distal tip of the helical hairpin is disordered (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 1A.

claim: In the Munc18–Stx complex, the domain 3a helical hairpin adopts a furled conformation in which the distal tip folds back on the more proximal portion, concealing the R-SNARE binding site.
source: In the Munc18–Stx complex, it adopts a furled conformation in which the distal tip folds back on the more proximal portion, concealing the R-SNARE binding site (Misura et al., 2000; Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This is based on the Munc18-Stx structure and shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: The bound syntaxin-1 sterically blocks unfurling of the Munc18 domain 3a helical hairpin.
source: The bound Stx, moreover, sterically blocks unfurling (Baker and Hughson, 2016; Hu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations.

claim: In the structures of Vps33 bound to the SNARE motifs of Vam3 and Nyv1, the helical hairpin adopts an unfurled, extended conformation.
source: In the structures of Vps33 bound to the SNARE motifs of Vam3 and Nyv1, by contrast, the helical hairpin adopts an unfurled, extended conformation (Figure 4B) that interacts extensively with the Qa- and R-SNARE respectively (Baker et al., 2015; Figure 4C).
evidence: This is based on the Vps33 structures and shown in Figure 4B,C.

claim: An unfurled conformation of the domain 3a helical hairpin is also seen in the Vps45–Tlg2 complex.
source: An unfurled conformation is also seen in the Vps45–Tlg2 complex (Figures 1A and 4), made possible by the open conformation of the bound Qa-SNARE (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figures 1A and 4.

claim: The unfurled conformation of the domain 3a helical hairpin is made possible by the open conformation of the bound Qa-SNARE.
source: An unfurled conformation is also seen in the Vps45–Tlg2 complex (Figures 1A and 4), made possible by the open conformation of the bound Qa-SNARE (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural comparison.

claim: The strong similarity between the unfurled Vps33 and Vps45 hairpins suggests that the unfurled conformation may be a well-defined active conformation.
source: The strong similarity between the unfurled Vps33 and Vps45 hairpins (Figure 4B) suggests that the unfurled conformation may be a well-defined active conformation.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural comparison shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The authors were unable to identify in vitro conditions under which C. thermophilum Tlg2, with or without Vps45, assembles into SNARE complexes.
source: Unfortunately, we were unable to identify in vitro conditions under which C. thermophilum Tlg2, with or without Vps45, assembles into SNARE complexes.
evidence: This is reported in the Results section.

claim: Based on the crystal structure, the Vps45–Tlg2 complex appears to be primed to bind an R-SNARE.
source: Nonetheless, based on the crystal structure, the Vps45–Tlg2 complex appears to be primed to bind an R-SNARE and, as demonstrated for SM proteins of the Sec1/Munc18 and Vps33 families (Jiao et al., 2018), to catalyze SNARE assembly (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is inferred from the structure and comparison with other SM proteins.

claim: The domain 3a helical hairpin in the Vps45–Tlg2 structure participates in crystal contacts that could potentially influence its conformation.
source: A caveat to the above conclusions is that, as observed previously in other SM protein structures (Baker et al., 2015; Hu et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2020), the domain 3a helical hairpin in the Vps45–Tlg2 structure participates in crystal contacts that could potentially influence its conformation.
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure and noted as a caveat.

claim: The domain 3a helical hairpin interacts with the Tlg2 SNARE motif (layers –8 to –4) of a crystallographically adjacent Vps45–Tlg2 complex.
source: Specifically, the hairpin interacts with the Tlg2 SNARE motif (layers –8 to –4) of a crystallographically adjacent Vps45–Tlg2 complex (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A–D.

claim: The hairpin mutant Vps45(V306D,F335R) formed stable complexes with Tlg2 that crystallized in a new space group.
source: The hairpin mutant Vps45V306D,F335R formed stable complexes with Tlg2 that crystallized in a new space group (Table 1).
evidence: This is reported in the Results section and Table 1.

claim: Crystals of Vps45(V306D,F335R)–Tlg2 diffracted only to about 5 Å resolution.
source: Although these crystals diffracted only to about 5 Å resolution, electron density maps phased by molecular replacement with a model of Vps45–Tlg2 lacking the SNARE motif allowed us to reach two unambiguous conclusions.
evidence: This is reported in the Results section and Table 1.

claim: In the Vps45(V306D,F335R)–Tlg2 structure, layers –8 to –4 of the Tlg2 SNARE motif no longer interact with the helical hairpin.
source: First, layers –8 to –4 of the Tlg2 SNARE motif no longer interact with the helical hairpin, instead curving away to make a minor crystallographic contact with the SNARE motif of a neighboring Tlg2 molecule (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is observed in the electron density map shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: In the Vps45(V306D,F335R)–Tlg2 structure, the remainder of the structure—including the position of the Habc domain and the unfurled helical hairpin—appears to be unchanged.
source: Second, while electron density at this resolution cannot reveal subtle differences, the remainder of the structure—including the position of the Habc domain and the unfurled helical hairpin—appears to be unchanged.
evidence: This is observed in the electron density map.

claim: C. thermophilum Vps45–Tlg2 forms a 1:1 complex.
source: Although C. thermophilum Vps45–Tlg2 forms a 1:1 complex, the maltose binding protein tagged full-length cytoplasmic region of Tlg2 (MBP-Tlg21-327) formed oligomers as judged by size exclusion chromatography (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography.

claim: The maltose binding protein tagged full-length cytoplasmic region of Tlg2 (MBP-Tlg2(1-327)) formed oligomers as judged by size exclusion chromatography.
source: Although C. thermophilum Vps45–Tlg2 forms a 1:1 complex, the maltose binding protein tagged full-length cytoplasmic region of Tlg2 (MBP-Tlg21-327) formed oligomers as judged by size exclusion chromatography (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: The Tlg2 SNARE motif (MBP-Tlg2(258-327)) formed oligomers.
source: The Tlg2 SNARE motif (MBP-Tlg2258-327) likewise formed oligomers, whereas the MBP-tagged SNARE motifs from the cognate R-, Qb-, and Qc-SNAREs (Snc2, Vti1, and Tlg1) did not (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The MBP-tagged SNARE motifs from the cognate R-, Qb-, and Qc-SNAREs (Snc2, Vti1, and Tlg1) did not form oligomers.
source: The Tlg2 SNARE motif (MBP-Tlg2258-327) likewise formed oligomers, whereas the MBP-tagged SNARE motifs from the cognate R-, Qb-, and Qc-SNAREs (Snc2, Vti1, and Tlg1) did not (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Tlg2 oligomerization is driven by the formation of SNARE complex-like bundles of SNARE motifs.
source: These observations suggested that Tlg2 oligomerization, like Stx oligomerization (Lerman et al., 2000; Misura et al., 2001), is driven by the formation of SNARE complex-like bundles of SNARE motifs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the SNARE motif alone oligomerizes, and supported by comparison to syntaxin-1.

claim: Sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation analysis of both MBP-tagged and untagged Tlg2(258-327) showed that the Tlg2 SNARE motif behaves as a single species with an apparent molecular mass indicative of a tetramer.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, sedimentation velocity analytical ultracentrifugation analysis of both MBP-tagged and untagged Tlg2258-327 showed that the Tlg2 SNARE motif behaves as a single species with an apparent molecular mass indicative of a tetramer (Figure 5D,F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analytical ultracentrifugation shown in Figure 5D,F and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: When MBP-Tlg2(1-327) was mixed with an equimolar amount of Vps45 and incubated for 2 hr, the majority of the Vps45 shifted into two higher molecular weight peaks.
source: After a 2 hr incubation, the majority of the Vps45 shifted into two higher molecular weight peaks, one of them likely representing Vps45 bound to MBP-Tlg21-327 oligomers, the other representing the 1:1 Vps45–MBP-Tlg21-327 complex (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At longer incubation times, the 1:1 Vps45–MBP-Tlg2(1-327) complex peak became more prominent at the expense of the peak representing Vps45 bound to MBP-Tlg2(1-327) oligomers.
source: At longer incubation times, the 1:1 complex peak became more prominent at the expense of the peak representing Vps45 bound to MBP-Tlg21-327 oligomers, and the Vps45-only peak disappeared altogether.
evidence: This is demonstrated by time-course size exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Vps45 is able to rescue MBP-Tlg2(1-327) from the oligomeric state, presumably by trapping MBP-Tlg2(1-327) monomers that transiently dissociate.
source: These data imply that Vps45 is able to rescue MBP-Tlg21-327 from the oligomeric state, presumably by trapping MBP-Tlg21-327 monomers that transiently dissociate (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is inferred from the time-course size exclusion chromatography data.

claim: The N-peptide (MBP-Tlg2(1-20)) bound to Vps45.
source: As expected, the N-peptide (MBP-Tlg21-20) bound to Vps45 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The N-peptide:Vps45 interaction appears to underlie the ability of Vps45 to rescue Tlg2 from oligomers.
source: The N-peptide:Vps45 interaction appears to underlie the ability of Vps45 to rescue Tlg2 from oligomers, since N-terminally truncated Tlg2 constructs (MBP-Tlg221-327 and MBP-Tlg2258-327) formed oligomers that neither bound to nor were rescued by Vps45 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that N-terminally truncated Tlg2 constructs are not rescued by Vps45.

claim: N-terminally truncated Tlg2 constructs (MBP-Tlg2(21-327) and MBP-Tlg2(258-327)) formed oligomers that neither bound to nor were rescued by Vps45.
source: The N-peptide:Vps45 interaction appears to underlie the ability of Vps45 to rescue Tlg2 from oligomers, since N-terminally truncated Tlg2 constructs (MBP-Tlg221-327 and MBP-Tlg2258-327) formed oligomers that neither bound to nor were rescued by Vps45 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is demonstrated by size exclusion chromatography shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The structure of the Vps45–Tlg2 complex is strikingly different from the Munc18–Stx complex.
source: The structure reported here, of the almost full-length cytoplasmic domain of Tlg2 bound to Vps45, is strikingly different.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from comparing the two structures.

claim: In the Vps45–Tlg2 structure, the bound SNARE adopts a much more open conformation than in the Munc18–Stx complex, with only a glancing interaction between the Habc domain and the SNARE motif.
source: Rather than a four-helix-bundle-like closed conformation, the bound SNARE adopts a much more open conformation, with only a glancing interaction between the Habc domain and the SNARE motif (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is observed in the crystal structure shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The linker between the Habc domain and the SNARE motif in the Munc18–Stx complex is a target for Munc13's syntaxin-1-opening activity.
source: The linker between the Habc domain and the SNARE motif, which in the Munc18–Stx complex is a target for Munc13's Stx-opening activity (Dulubova et al., 1999; Lai et al., 2017; Ma et al., 2011; Misura et al., 2000; Wang et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2020; Yang et al., 2015), appears to be disordered.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The domain 3a helical hairpin is furled in the Munc18–Stx complex but unfurled in the Vps45–Tlg2 complex.
source: Finally, the domain 3a helical hairpin, which plays a crucial role in SNARE templating (Baker et al., 2015; Boyd et al., 2008; Hu et al., 2011; Jiao et al., 2018; Parisotto et al., 2014; Sitarska et al., 2017), is furled in the Munc18–Stx complex but unfurled—and therefore primed for R-SNARE binding—in the Vps45–Tlg2 complex (Figure 4).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the structures shown in Figure 4.

claim: There have been conflicting reports regarding the tendency of yeast Tlg2 to oligomerize and/or form a closed conformation.
source: There have been conflicting reports regarding the tendency of yeast Tlg2 to oligomerize and/or form a closed conformation (Dulubova et al., 2002; Furgason et al., 2009; Struthers et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to conflicting reports.

claim: The SNARE motif of C. thermophilum Tlg2 unambiguously forms tetramers.
source: The SNARE motif of C. thermophilum Tlg2, however, unambiguously forms tetramers (Figure 5D,F).
evidence: This is demonstrated by analytical ultracentrifugation shown in Figure 5D,F.

claim: The SNARE motif of syntaxin-1, by forming four-helix bundles, can drive the formation of off-pathway products requiring rescue by NSF/α-SNAP and Munc18.
source: In this respect it resembles the SNARE motif of Stx which, by forming four-helix bundles, can drive the formation of off-pathway products requiring rescue by NSF/α-SNAP and Munc18 (Ma et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Ma et al., 2013.

claim: In both Munc18–Stx and Vps45–Tlg2, binding to the cognate SM protein prevents SNARE oligomerization.
source: In both instances, binding to the cognate SM protein prevents SNARE oligomerization.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing that Vps45 prevents Tlg2 oligomerization, and from previous work on Munc18-Stx.

claim: For Munc18–Stx, the protective effect against oligomerization has been attributed to the closed conformation of syntaxin-1.
source: For Munc18–Stx, this protective effect has been attributed to the closed conformation of Stx.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: In the Vps45–Tlg2 structure, Tlg2 is open but nevertheless protected from oligomerization.
source: In the Vps45–Tlg2 structure, Tlg2 is open but nevertheless protected from oligomerization.
evidence: This is observed in the structure and biochemical data.

claim: Protection from oligomerization in the Vps45–Tlg2 complex arises from binding of the SM protein to layers 0 to +4 of the SNARE motif.
source: We propose that this protection arises from binding of the SM protein to layers 0 to +4 of the SNARE motif (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is proposed based on the structural observation shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The other principal interaction between Vps45 and Tlg2, involving the Tlg2 N-peptide, increases the stability of the Vps45–Tlg2 complex but would not seem capable of preventing SNARE motif self-association.
source: The other principal interaction between Vps45 and Tlg2, involving the Tlg2 N-peptide, increases the stability of the Vps45–Tlg2 complex but would not seem capable of preventing SNARE motif self-association.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data and the observation that N-terminally truncated Tlg2 is not rescued by Vps45.

claim: The Tlg2 N-peptide plays a key role by equipping the Tlg2 tetramers with exposed, high-affinity handles for Vps45 to grab onto.
source: The Tlg2 N-peptide nevertheless plays a key role, by equipping the Tlg2 tetramers with exposed, high-affinity (27 nM for the mammalian orthologues [Burkhardt et al., 2008]) handles for Vps45 to grab onto (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is inferred from the data and supported by citation to Burkhardt et al., 2008.

claim: The affinity of the N-peptide for Vps45 is 27 nM for the mammalian orthologues.
source: The Tlg2 N-peptide nevertheless plays a key role, by equipping the Tlg2 tetramers with exposed, high-affinity (27 nM for the mammalian orthologues [Burkhardt et al., 2008]) handles for Vps45 to grab onto (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Burkhardt et al., 2008.

claim: Vps45 can rescue Tlg2 from off-pathway oligomers and hold it in an open, non-oligomerization-prone state in preparation for SNARE complex assembly.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that Vps45 can rescue Tlg2 from off-pathway oligomers and hold it in an open, non-oligomerization-prone state in preparation for SNARE complex assembly (Figure 7).
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the structural and biochemical data, illustrated in Figure 7.

claim: Template complexes containing half-zippered Qa- and R-SNAREs bound to the cognate SM protein are essential intermediates in SM-catalyzed SNARE assembly.
source: Template complexes containing half-zippered Qa- and R-SNAREs bound to the cognate SM protein are essential intermediates in SM-catalyzed SNARE assembly (Baker et al., 2015; Jiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Baker et al., 2015 and Jiao et al., 2018.

claim: Yeast Vps45 was reported to bind the R-SNARE Snc2.
source: Yeast Vps45 was reported to bind the R-SNARE Snc2, but the relevance of this observation to the potential formation of a template complex is uncertain since Tlg2 appeared to displace the Vps45-bound Snc2 (Carpp et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Carpp et al., 2006.

claim: The relevance of Vps45 binding to Snc2 to the potential formation of a template complex is uncertain since Tlg2 appeared to displace the Vps45-bound Snc2.
source: Yeast Vps45 was reported to bind the R-SNARE Snc2, but the relevance of this observation to the potential formation of a template complex is uncertain since Tlg2 appeared to displace the Vps45-bound Snc2 (Carpp et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Carpp et al., 2006.

claim: The close structural resemblance between the unfurled helical hairpins of Tlg2-bound Vps45, Vam3-bound Vps33, and Nyv1-bound Vps33 strongly suggests that Tlg2-bound Vps45 is primed for R-SNARE binding.
source: Nonetheless, the close structural resemblance between the unfurled helical hairpins of Tlg2-bound Vps45, Vam3-bound Vps33, and Nyv1-bound Vps33, together with the ability of Vps33, Nyv1, and Vam3 to form a ternary complex (Baker et al., 2015), strongly suggests that Tlg2-bound Vps45 is primed for R-SNARE binding (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is inferred from the structural comparison and supported by citation to Baker et al., 2015.

claim: Vps45 binding to the R-SNARE need not be high affinity in order to promote SNARE assembly.
source: This binding need not be high affinity in order to promote SNARE assembly; indeed, Munc18 binding to the R-SNARE VAMP2/synaptobrevin is weak (Sitarska et al., 2017) but nonetheless critical for forming the template complex (Jiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sitarska et al., 2017 and Jiao et al., 2018.

claim: Munc18 binding to the R-SNARE VAMP2/synaptobrevin is weak but nonetheless critical for forming the template complex.
source: This binding need not be high affinity in order to promote SNARE assembly; indeed, Munc18 binding to the R-SNARE VAMP2/synaptobrevin is weak (Sitarska et al., 2017) but nonetheless critical for forming the template complex (Jiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sitarska et al., 2017 and Jiao et al., 2018.

claim: The stringent regulation of neurotransmitter release requires the control of synaptic SNARE complex formation by Munc18 and Munc13-1.
source: The stringent regulation of neurotransmitter release requires the control of synaptic SNARE complex formation by Munc18, which clamps Stx in an inactive closed conformation, and Munc13-1, which mediates Stx opening (Brunger et al., 2018; Rizo, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brunger et al., 2018 and Rizo, 2018.

claim: Munc18 clamps syntaxin-1 in an inactive closed conformation.
source: The stringent regulation of neurotransmitter release requires the control of synaptic SNARE complex formation by Munc18, which clamps Stx in an inactive closed conformation, and Munc13-1, which mediates Stx opening (Brunger et al., 2018; Rizo, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brunger et al., 2018 and Rizo, 2018.

claim: Munc13-1 mediates syntaxin-1 opening.
source: The stringent regulation of neurotransmitter release requires the control of synaptic SNARE complex formation by Munc18, which clamps Stx in an inactive closed conformation, and Munc13-1, which mediates Stx opening (Brunger et al., 2018; Rizo, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Brunger et al., 2018 and Rizo, 2018.

claim: The Vps45–Tlg2 structure reveals a new mode of interaction in which the Qa-SNARE is held open rather than clamped shut.
source: Our Vps45–Tlg2 structure reveals a new mode of interaction in which the Qa-SNARE is held open rather than clamped shut.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the structural data.

claim: It is possible that the open mode of SM-SNARE interaction is the rule, with the Munc18–Stx mode being the exception.
source: It is possible that this new mode is the rule, with the Munc18–Stx mode being the exception.
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural comparison.

claim: The task of Munc13-1 may be to convert the Munc18–Stx complex into a Vps45–Tlg2-like conformation.
source: It is furthermore attractive to speculate that the task of Munc13-1 is to convert the Munc18–Stx complex into a Vps45–Tlg2-like conformation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural comparison.

claim: A principal difference between closed syntaxin-1 and open Tlg2 is the linker between the Habc domain and the SNARE motif, which is folded in the first case and unfolded in the second.
source: Notably, a principal difference between closed Stx and open Tlg2 is the linker between the Habc domain and the SNARE motif, which is folded in the first case and unfolded in the second (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the structures shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Munc13-1, by binding to the Munc18–Stx complex and destabilizing the Stx linker, may promote the conformational switch that allows Stx to open, the domain 3a helical hairpin to unfurl, and the template complex to form.
source: Munc13-1, by binding to the Munc18–Stx complex and destabilizing the Stx linker (Lai et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2020), may thereby promote the conformational switch that allows Stx to open, the domain 3a helical hairpin to unfurl, and the template complex to form.
evidence: This is speculation based on the structural comparison and supported by citations.
